item.description: This article summarizes ten common techniques of psychological manipulation used by cults, Nazis, and dictators, and proposes corresponding countermeasures, with the aim of raising public awareness and preventing the recurrence of historical tragedies.
item.content:encoded:
In the long river of human history, there have been numerous cults, Nazis, and dictators who, through various means, have manipulated the minds of the people and consolidated their rule, bringing severe disasters to society. Looking at their common methods, although the forms are diverse, their essence shares many similarities. Below, we summarize ten common tricks, hoping to warn future generations and prevent them from repeating the same mistakes.

Their Methods

1. Deification Movement: Shaping Absolute Authority

This is the foundation of all authoritarian rule. Through various propaganda means, the leader is molded into an image of omnipotence, brilliance, and martial prowess, often even endowed with supernatural abilities, making them a “god” in the eyes of the populace. This creation of personal worship aims to strip the people of their independent thinking ability, forcing them to blindly obey the leader’s will.

2. Information Monopoly: Controlling the Source of Thought

Information is the carrier of thought. By controlling channels of information dissemination—such as media, publishing, and the internet—and monopolizing the release and spread of information, only data conforming to the ruler’s wishes is allowed to circulate. This is used to shape public opinion and control the people’s thoughts.

3. Suppressing Freedom of Speech: Stifling the Voice of Dissent

Freedom of speech is the guarantee of freedom of thought. By suppressing freedom of speech and prohibiting any criticism or questioning of the rulers, dissent is stifled through intimidation, censorship, and even violence, creating a situation where all voices are muted.

4. Promising Utopia: Painting an Illusory Future

By depicting a beautiful future—such as a “Communist Paradise” or a “Millennium Empire”—rulers stimulate the hope and enthusiasm of the people, thereby masking the cruelty of reality and the true nature of the regime. This false promise often becomes a crucial tool for the rulers to deceive the masses.

5. Creating Enemies and Inciting Hatred: Shifting the Focus of Conflict

By artificially establishing one or more “enemies”—such as “hostile foreign forces,” “counter-revolutionaries,” or “heretics”—the social conflict is shifted onto these “enemies,” and the people are incited to hate them. This serves to consolidate internal strength and maintain the rule.

6. Controlling Education and Cultural Propaganda: Systemic Brainwashing

By controlling the education system, single-minded ideological indoctrination is carried out from a young age, ensuring that the people accept predetermined values and ideologies. Simultaneously, various propaganda tools are utilized to conduct massive positive publicity, shaping the glorious image of the leader and disseminating favorable narratives for the rulers.

7. Benevolence and Might (Carrot and Stick): The Dual Strategy of Rule

For the compliant, rewards and favors are given; for the resistors, severe punishment and suppression are employed. This “carrot and stick” strategy effectively controls the behavior of the populace, making them hesitant to challenge the ruler’s authority easily.

8. Utilizing Times of Crisis or Turmoil: Seizing the Opportunity

When society faces a crisis or turmoil, the people often feel anxious and lost. At this time, cults, Nazis, and dictators are more likely to exploit this psychological state by offering seemingly effective solutions or promises, thereby gaining support and power.

9. Establishing Strict Organization and Hierarchy: Ensuring Power Concentration

By establishing a strict organizational structure and hierarchy, power is concentrated in the hands of the leader, and it is ensured that commands are effectively transmitted and executed. This pyramidal power structure allows the leader to exert effective control over the organization.

10. Emphasizing Collectivism and Suppressing Individualism: Erasing Individual Independence

Emphasizing that collective interests are paramount and that the individual must submit to the collective. This ideology effectively suppresses individual consciousness and independent thought, making the individual a tool of the collective, thereby serving the rulers better.

11. Divide and Conquer

By encouraging internal strife, tribalism, or distrust, the potential opposition groups are encouraged to split apart, ensuring that a unified resistance cannot form.

These methods do not exist in isolation; rather, they are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, collectively forming a tight control system. Recognizing and being vigilant against these tricks helps us maintain a clear mind, preventing us from being deceived and exploited, and jointly safeguarding the values of freedom and democracy. Only through continuous reflection and vigilance can we maximize the avoidance of historical tragedies.

Countermeasures

1. Cultivating Critical Thinking: Not Blindly Following, But Thinking Deeply

  • Questioning Authority: Do not easily accept any unverified information, especially propaganda from official channels. Cultivate the habit of independent thinking, maintaining a degree of skepticism toward any information, and not blindly trusting authority.
  • Thinking from Multiple Angles: Try to view issues from different perspectives and seek various sources of information. Do not accept a single explanation; instead, try to understand as many different viewpoints and positions as possible to form a comprehensive understanding.
  • Logical Reasoning: Learning basic knowledge of logic, such as identifying common logical fallacies, helps in discerning the loopholes in false information and propaganda slogans.

2. Expanding Information Sources: Breaking the Information Cocoon

  • Using VPNs/Circumvention Tools (If Possible): Although there are risks, using tools like VPNs allows access to censored foreign information, providing a more comprehensive view and breaking the information blockade. Be sure to prioritize security, choose reputable VPN services, and protect personal privacy.
  • Following Independent Media and Commentators: Look for independent media and commentators who often provide perspectives and views different from official propaganda. However, also be mindful of verifying the truthfulness of the information and maintaining critical thinking.
  • Interacting with People from Different Backgrounds: Communicating with people from different backgrounds and with different views helps expand your horizons, understand diverse perspectives, and avoid falling into a single mode of thinking.

3. Protecting Personal Privacy: Speaking Cautiously, Paying Attention to Cybersecurity

  • Avoiding Sensitive Remarks in Public: In a high-pressure environment, one must speak carefully and cautiously, avoiding making any remarks that might cause trouble in public, including on social media.
  • Using Secure Communication Tools: Use encrypted communication software for private exchanges to prevent personal information from being monitored.
  • Paying Attention to Cybersecurity: Regularly change passwords, avoid clicking on unknown links, and prevent personal information leakage.

4. Learning History: Learning from the Past to Avoid Repeating Mistakes

  • Understanding the History of Totalitarianism: By reading history books and watching documentaries, one can understand the operation and dangers of totalitarianism, thereby increasing vigilance and avoiding past mistakes.
  • Focusing on Human Rights and Freedom: Paying attention to the international community’s focus on human rights and freedom, and understanding related laws and systems, helps in better protecting one’s own rights.

5. Maintaining Physical and Mental Health: Preserving Mental Independence

  • Maintaining an Optimistic Mindset: In a high-pressure environment, maintaining an optimistic mindset is crucial. Stress can be relieved through exercise, meditation, and other methods, helping to maintain physical and mental health.
  • Seeking Support: If feeling excessive stress, one can seek help and support from friends, family, or professionals.

6. Accumulating Strength, Waiting for the Opportunity: Never Giving Up Hope

  • Do Not Despair: Even in the darkest times, maintain hope, believing that change will eventually come.
  • Accumulating Strength: Within one’s personal capacity, do things that can be done, such as spreading the truth or supporting vulnerable groups.
  • Monitoring Social Changes: Closely observe social changes, waiting for the appropriate moment.

Important Tips:

  • Safety is always the priority. Before taking any action, be sure to carefully assess the risks and take necessary safety measures.
  • Do not try to fight the powerful totalitarian machine alone. Protecting yourself, accumulating strength, and waiting for the right time is the wiser choice.
  • These suggestions are designed to help individuals maintain independent thinking, protect themselves, and accumulate strength for future change in a high-pressure environment. Remember, even in the darkest moments, maintain hope, believing that light will eventually come.

item.description: Don't assume that the highest echelon is omnipotent. The Emperor is merely a mortal, incapable of controlling the entire world.
item.content:encoded:
The entire shift from rice to mulberry was implemented, and the cabinet was merely a figurehead; everything was decided solely by Emperor Jiajing.

  • The decision was hasty
  • The methods were intense
  • The effects were extreme
  • The result was poorly executed (or: unfinished/aborted)

Therefore, when we make decisions, we must take this into account. We cannot assume that the intentions above will definitely be realized; nothing is omnipotent, and there will always be difficulties. There is no omnipotent god in the world, and the central bank, with its infinite capital, is no exception.

  • The decrease in corporate revenue leads to a decline in employee income and tax revenue.

Historical Lessons

Historical Lessons

This situation is bound to lead to extreme changes, which is unacceptable, so countermeasures must be taken. What is the goal of these countermeasures? Naturally, it is to maintain social stability, and on this point, everyone’s interests are aligned.

Current Solutions

1. Monetary Policy Intervention

  • Quantitative Easing (QE): They can instruct the central bank to inject large-scale currency, increasing market liquidity. This approach can rapidly boost asset prices, stimulate consumption, and create the illusion of economic prosperity.
  • Lowering Interest Rates: By lowering interest rates, they encourage borrowing by individuals and corporations, promoting investment and consumption, thereby stimulating economic activity.

2. Fiscal Policy Stimulus

  • Increasing Government Spending: They can increase spending through government projects and infrastructure construction to create jobs and promote economic growth. This investment can yield quick results and enhance public support for the government.
  • Tax Reduction: Reducing the tax burden in the short term increases disposable income for consumers, stimulating consumption and thereby promoting economic growth.

3. Market Manipulation

  • Stock Market Manipulation: By various means (e.g., the central bank directly purchasing stocks) to lift the stock market, creating a wealth effect, making the middle class and asset holders feel wealthy, thereby increasing consumption and investment.
  • Real Estate Market Stimulation: Lowering mortgage interest rates or providing housing subsidies to promote the recovery of the real estate market, thereby driving the development of related industries.

4. Information Manipulation

  • Propaganda and Public Opinion Control: Shaping a positive economic image through the propaganda machine, reducing public attention to economic problems, and enhancing public trust and support for the government.
  • Data Manipulation: Manipulating economic indicators and releasing optimistic economic data to create the illusion of economic prosperity.

5. Suppressing Social Dissatisfaction

  • Suppressing Dissenting Voices: By severely suppressing protests and opposition parties, maintaining surface-level social stability, and preventing the outbreak of social unrest and dissatisfaction.
  • Providing Short-Term Welfare: Providing some short-term economic aid or subsidies to low-income groups to alleviate livelihood pressure and gain public support.

6. Increasing State Control

Nationalization or Control of Key Industries: Achieving national interests and regime stability by controlling key economic sectors. This can help them better cope with crises during economic difficulties.

Conclusion Through these short-term or medium-term strategies, they can effectively maintain superficial prosperity and stability during an economic recession, strengthening their foundation of rule.

item.title: Law of Blood Compensation
item.description: The prerequisite for robbery is that there must be something to steal; the prerequisite for kidnapping and demanding ransom is that the hostage must have the financial capacity to pay the ransom. As the Law of Blood Payment (or Law of Life Compensation) states, the value of the hostage’s life is determined by the willingness and ability of the parties to pay the ransom. Under conditions of equal risk and cost, the richer the hostage, and the wealthier the target of the robbery, the higher the profit from the kidnapping and robbery. Conversely, the poorer the target of the robbery and kidnapping, the lower the profit from the robbery. If the profit is so low that it is not worth the effort, the bandits cannot proceed.

item.title: Throughout all dynasties and generations, ancient and modern, domestic and international, it is all disaster springing from the mouth.

Galileo said those words, and as a result, he faced judgment from the religious court.

Nerds/Bookworms are the kind of people who get into trouble like that.

They wear unpopular clothes and speak inappropriate words.

They feel they have expressed the correct viewpoint, but in reality, they attract trouble.

The power of custom is not enough to restrain them.

The norm of history seems to be that people in any era firmly believe in some absurd things.

Their beliefs are very strong; as long as someone shows even a slight doubt, they will attract great trouble. Is our era different? If you have read a little history, you know the answer is almost certainly “no difference.”

Even if there is that tiny possibility, for the first time in history, that all the beliefs of our era are correct, it is due to astonishing coincidence, not because we have truly found the correct direction.

When one thinks that what we assert with certainty now is seen as absurd by people in the future, how can one not be amazed!

item.title: What is it that we cannot say?
item.description:
First, we can look at how people get into trouble because of what they say.

Only if two conditions are met simultaneously.

The first condition is that the words cannot be said;

The second condition is that they are correct, or seem likely to be correct and are worth further discussion. If the second condition is not met, in most cases, you won’t have trouble.

If you say that 2+2 equals 5, or that the average height of a citizen in Pittsburgh is three meters, you won’t have any issues. These obviously incorrect statements might be taken as a joke, or worse, as proof that you are crazy, but they certainly won’t anger anyone.

item.title: Zhu Yuanzhang used the Yellow Registers (Huangce) and Travel Permits (Luyin) to confine farmers to the land. Why did these policies become ineffective later?
item.description:
In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the development of the socio-economy and population growth, farmers’ demand for land increased. However, the uneven distribution of land and the heavy burden of taxes made it impossible for many farmers to maintain a livelihood. Therefore, they began seeking ways to improve their lives, such as temporary registration (jiji), wandering/migrating (youyu), or engaging in maritime commerce (xiahai jingshang) 12.

In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the corruption of officials and lax supervision, the management of the Yellow Registers and travel permits became chaotic and riddled with loopholes. Phenomena such as fraudulent registration (maoji), fake household registration (jiaji), and privately manufactured travel permits were frequently observed, causing the household registration system to lose its regulatory power 12.

item.title: What are the defining changes as a dynasty moves from its middle phase to its final years?
item.description:
As a dynasty moves from its middle period towards its late years, it is often accompanied by a series of characteristic changes. Here are some common changes:

Political Instability and Power Struggles: As time passes, the dynasty’s governance often experiences instability and power struggles. Political corruption, unfair official appointments, and the phenomenon of vying for power may intensify, leading to internal political instability and chaos.

Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.

Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.

Economic Decline and Fiscal Difficulties: The late years of a dynasty are often accompanied by economic recession and financial hardship. Reduced tax revenue and insufficient fiscal income to support national operations lead to rising prices, heavier taxation, and social poverty. Economic difficulties may result in social instability and public dissatisfaction.

Social Unrest and Popular Uprisings: With the arrival of the late dynasty, social unrest and popular uprisings may occur frequently. Phenomena such as peasant rebellions, waves of migration, and local fragmentation (or regional warlordism) may intensify, posing a serious threat to the stability of the central government. These uprisings and unrest are often a strong resistance against government corruption, exploitation, and oppression.

Cultural Decline and Knowledge Atrophy: The late dynasty is often accompanied by cultural decline and intellectual atrophy. Fields such as academic research, literary arts, and technological innovation may be negatively affected, and the social cultural life and knowledge inheritance are suppressed.

These changes are common characteristics of a dynasty’s late years, but the specific situation varies depending on the history, region, and specific dynasty. The late years of a dynasty are often a stage of decline and demise, bearing obvious signs of recession and collapse.

item.title: Why are the late years of a dynasty often accompanied by economic decline and fiscal difficulties?
item.description:
There are multiple factors that can lead to the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty:

Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.

Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.

Excessive Taxation and Intensified Exploitation: To fill the fiscal deficit, the imperial court often increases the burden of taxes and the collection of other tribute goods. This places a heavy burden on farmers and merchants, leading to hindered economic development, decreased productivity, and even sparking social discontent and protests.

Obstruction of Domestic and International Trade and Market Contraction: The late dynasty often faces issues of obstructed domestic and international trade. Internal unrest and external wars lead to the interruption of transportation and trade routes, affecting the circulation of goods and the development of the market economy. Market contraction reduces commercial activities, further exacerbating the economic decline.

Decline in Agricultural Production and Frequent Disasters: Agriculture is the foundation of a dynastic economy, but at the end of a dynasty, agricultural production often declines. Factors such as long-term warfare, land abandonment, and peasant uprisings lead to a decrease in agricultural productivity. Simultaneously, natural disasters such as drought, floods, and locust plagues occur frequently, resulting in reduced or destroyed crops, further weakening the economic foundation.

Social Instability and Warfare Affecting Investment and Development: The late dynasty is often accompanied by social instability and warfare. Turbulent situations, such as internal rebellions, external threats, and peasant uprisings, hinder investment and development. Merchants and landlords may be reluctant to invest in economic development or transfer their assets, leading to a decline in economic vitality.

These factors interact to cause the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty. The combination of rulers’ negligence and political corruption, excessive taxation and exploitation, trade obstruction, agricultural decline, and social upheaval collectively leads to economic distress and fiscal collapse.

item.title: The Emperor is a terrorist
item.description: Fear makes bureaucracy more efficient, makes the common people more disciplined, makes the ruler’s benevolence easier for people to remember, and thus makes the ruler safer. Machiavelli says, “It is safer to be feared than to be loved.” A monarch who does not know how to “establish authority through killing” will eventually be looked down upon by the governed. Furthermore, benevolence and tolerance are only cherished and praised by the people when set against a backdrop of terror and severity. Therefore, a successful ruler must possess two sides: one side is the benevolence of a saint, the other is the cruelty of a lion.

item.description: As early as the Ming Dynasty, village heads and street entrances across various regions were erected with “Six Precepts Lying Steles” (or “Six Teachings Reclining Steles”). item.title: To seize when favorable, and to defend when unfavorable.
item.description: Before ascending the throne, Zhu’s forces were always the “Army of Benevolence and Righteousness” (Renyi Zhi Shi), and Zhu himself was always a model of practicing the “King’s Way” (Wang Dao). Consequently, the people willingly submitted their hearts and allegiance. Who would have thought that after conquering the realm and incorporating the entire populace into his cage, he would transform from being generous and benevolent to being harsh and cruel, raising the whip and the butcher’s knife to slaughter the world, massacring meritorious officials, and becoming a demonic king that made everyone tremble with fear? In fact, it was not Zhu Yuanzhang’s nature that changed, but the circumstances. Before ascending the throne, he sought support from various social classes; he needed to gain their backing. After ascending the throne, the common people had become the cattle and sheep under his pastoral care, and naturally, he was happy to command them forward with the butcher’s knife and the whip.
